title: the leap decided
hook: a hundred yojanas of water, and a circle of monkeys saying out loud how far each of them can jump
carry: no one could promise a hundred

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sampati, the old vulture whose wings grew back as he told the monkeys where Sita was. Across the sea, in Lanka. Your line was this is the sign that you'll succeed. Did you pass something useful on to someone? Today, the sea itself. Day six hundred two.

The job is finally clear, and it's impossible. The monkeys of the southern search party now know where Sita is. Sampati has told them: Lanka, an island a hundred yojanas across the ocean. A yojana is an old measure of distance, many miles long. They walk down to the shore and look at the water. Valmiki describes it the way you'd describe something alive: huge waves, sea creatures, a roar that never stops. And the whole army sits down on the sand, quiet. Nobody wants to say the obvious thing first.
screen: `THE JOB IS CLEAR.` → `A HUNDRED YOJANAS OF SEA.` → `THE ARMY SITS DOWN, QUIET.`

segments.voice: Angada, the young prince who leads them, breaks the silence. He asks a plain question: who here can cross this? Then, one by one, the monkeys answer honestly. Valmiki gives us the list. One says he can leap ten yojanas. Another, twenty. Another, thirty. And on it goes, each a little further, up to the old bear Jambavan, who says ninety. Jambavan adds a memory. When he was young, he says, he could have done it easily. He once circled the great god Vishnu when Vishnu strode across the worlds in three steps. But age has taken that from him. Then Angada speaks. He thinks he can jump the full hundred. What he isn't sure of is the jump back. Jambavan answers him kindly but firmly. You're the leader, he says, the root of the whole expedition. You don't send the root. Notice what this scene is doing. Nobody brags, and nobody pretends. Each monkey says what he can actually do, and the numbers fall short, and that's allowed. And it closes a week that took us from Svayamprabha's hidden cave, where the monkeys lost precious time underground, to Sampati, who lost his wings saving his brother and got them back by helping strangers, and now to a beach full of honest numbers that don't add up to a hundred. One monkey hasn't spoken. He's sitting apart, saying nothing at all.
screen: `WHO CAN CROSS THIS?` · `TEN, TWENTY, THIRTY... NINETY.` · `ANGADA: I'M NOT SURE OF THE WAY BACK.` · then, large: `YOU DON'T SEND THE ROOT.` · then: `ONE MONKEY HASN'T SPOKEN.`

segments.voice: Sit and let your breath settle. Bring to mind something in front of you right now that feels too far to cross: a task, a conversation, a long recovery. Instead of measuring the whole distance, ask yourself honestly how far you can go today. Ten yojanas? Twenty? Hold that number without shame. With each breath out, let the gap between what you can do and what is needed simply be true, for now. The bell holds the time.

Yojana, an old measure of distance many miles long. It's what the monkeys count in as each says how far he can jump, and the numbers fall short of a hundred, with the question of who will go still open.
Your line: no one could promise a hundred. Today, when someone asks what you can take on, give the honest number, not the impressive one. Day six hundred two.

screen: `DAY 602 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE LEAP DECIDED, PART TWO.`

howItsDone: Readers of the Kishkindha Kanda often linger on this scene of the monkeys stating their limits on the shore, because it sets up the moment when Jambavan turns to Hanuman.

pairs: asks who can cross the sea
told them Sita is in Lanka
an old measure of long distance

myth: every monkey claims he can jump the whole sea
each gives an honest, smaller number: ten, twenty, thirty, up to ninety.
Angada thinks he can reach Lanka but isn't sure he can get back
and Jambavan says the leader shouldn't be sent.
Jambavan once circled Vishnu as Vishnu strode the worlds
he remembers it as proof of how strong he used to be.

fork.setup: you're Jambavan. the prince says he'll make the jump himself. what do you say?
options: go, your highness, and good luck.
you're the root of this mission; we don't send the root.
fork.reveal: Jambavan refuses to send Angada: the leader is the root of the whole expedition, and someone else must go.

original.note: Sanskrit yojana, an old unit of distance; its exact length varies by source.

trapdoor: what you thought: the monkeys were all heroes who could do anything.
what it means: on the shore, each one names an honest limit, and none of the numbers reaches a hundred.
what a scholar hears: Jambavan's memory of circling Vishnu's three strides points to the Vamana story of Vishnu's three strides across the worlds, a story told in other Hindu texts as well.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 64–65 (the monkeys at the shore; how far each can leap)
